facts.text: Bogalusa was founded in 1906 by the Goodyear brothers and the Great Southern Lumber Company, its name taken from the nearby Bogue Lusa creek.
At its peak, Bogalusa operated one of the world’s largest sawmills, cementing its status as a lumber powerhouse.
The town was originally laid out with a “Mill Town” on the south side and a “Commercial Town” on the north, with racially segregated quadrants defined by the railroad and Bogue Lusa Creek.
In 1965, activists founded Bogalusa’s first Deacons for Defense chapter, a pivotal African‑American self‑defense organization during the civil rights era.
The Bogalusa Paper Mill Museum tells the story of the town’s lumber‑industry roots and its evolution into an industrial hub.
